answer:
Solve the 1D compressible Navier–Stokes equations (no heat conduction) in conservative form on x in [-1, 1] up to T = 0.5 with periodic boundary conditions.
Unknown fields are rho(x,t), v(x,t), p(x,t) with m = rho*v and E = p/(Gamma-1) + 0.5*rho*v^2.
The viscous stress is sigma = (zeta + 4/3*eta)*v_x with zeta = eta = 0.1.
The PDE system is: rho_t + (m)_x = 0; m_t + (m^2/rho + p - sigma)_x = 0; E_t + ((E+p)*v - v*sigma)_x = 0.
Use Gamma = 1.6666666666666667.
Interpret '^' as exponentiation in math and use '**' in Python code.
Use a cell-centered uniform finite-volume grid with Nx = 400 cells on [-1, 1], dx = 2/400 = 0.005, and cell centers x_j = -1 + (j+0.5)*dx for j = 0,...,399.
Evolve the conservative variables U = [rho, m, E] as cell averages.
Use the equation of state p = (Gamma-1)*(E - 0.5*m^2/rho) and clip rho and p to a floor of 1e-12 if needed to maintain positivity.
Use the Rusanov (local Lax-Friedrichs) numerical flux for the inviscid Euler part with F_conv(U) = [m, m^2/rho + p, (E+p)*v] and v = m/rho.
Compute the interface wave speed as a = max(|v_L| + c_L, |v_R| + c_R) with c = sqrt(Gamma*p/rho), and the numerical flux as F_hat = 0.5*(F_conv(U_L) + F_conv(U_R)) - 0.5*a*(U_R - U_L).
Compute v_x with a centered difference on the cell-centered v values, set sigma = (zeta + 4/3*eta)*v_x, and approximate sigma at interfaces by averaging neighboring cell-centered values.
Add the viscous flux F_visc = [0, -sigma, -v*sigma] at each interface using interface-averaged v and sigma, so the total interface flux is F_total = F_hat + F_visc.
Use CFL = 0.4 for the convective time step restriction.
Set dt each step as dt = min(dt_conv, dt_visc) with dt_conv = CFL*dx/max_j(|v_j| + c_j) and dt_visc = 0.5*dx^2/max(zeta + 4/3*eta, 1e-30), and shorten the last step so the final time T = 0.5 is hit exactly.
Advance in time with the 2-stage SSP-RK2 (Heun's method) applied to the semi-discrete finite-volume system.
Implement the periodic boundary conditions by wrapping indices.
Set the initial conditions pointwise on the cell centers: rho(x,0) = 1.0 + 0.2*sin(pi*x), v(x,0) = 0.1*cos(pi*x), p(x,0) = 1.0 + 0.2*cos(pi*x), using radians for trig.
Compute rho(x,T), v(x,T), p(x,T) on the cell centers at T = 0.5.
Save the solution to "solution_pdebench_cns1d_eta0p1_periodic_smooth.npz" containing arrays x (1D length Nx), rho (1D), v (1D), p (1D), and scalars Gamma, eta, zeta, T, dx, CFL.
Save a 3-panel (or 3 separate) line plot of rho, v, p versus x at T as "solution_pdebench_cns1d_eta0p1_periodic_smooth.png".
Print the min/max of rho and p as a positivity check and the mean of rho over the domain as a mass conservation check.
